title: How Gentle God's Commands
description: How Gentle God's Commands in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 258, “God Will Provide”. The compilers changed some of the words, and this is their version.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How gen-tle God's com-mands! How kind His pre-cepts are! Come, leave your bur-dens to the Lord, And trust His con-stant care.

lines: Come, leave your burdens to the Lord,
The hand that bears creation up
Come, seek your Heavenly Father's face,
We'll drop our burden at His feet,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
